about: PyPI (Python Package Index): look up Python packages and specific versions, read release, update and new-package RSS feeds, see top projects by size and index-wide totals, and fetch the GitHub repo stats and issues that PyPI project pages show.

commands.summary: Get a package's PyPI page for its latest version: name and version, summary, pip install command, project links and metadata sidebar, and README text.

params.name: name
params.description: Package name as it appears on PyPI, e.g. requests

commands.summary: Get the PyPI page for one specific version of a package: header, summary, pinned pip command, metadata sidebar and the README as it was at that release.
List a package's recent releases (version, link, publish date) from its releases RSS feed.
List the newest releases uploaded across all of PyPI (package + version, link, date) from the site-wide updates RSS feed.
List projects newly created on PyPI (name, link, summary, date) from the newest-packages RSS feed.
List the top 100 PyPI projects ranked by the total size of their release files. The first row is the total for all of PyPI.
Get PyPI-wide totals shown on the homepage (number of projects, releases, files, users).
Get the GitHub statistics PyPI shows for a project's source repo (stars, forks, open issues, description, last push), from the GitHub API.

params.name: owner
params.description: GitHub user or organization that owns the repo (from the package's Source link), e.g. psf

commands.summary: Search GitHub issues and PRs with a GitHub query, e.g. the open issues of a package's repo, via the GitHub search API (the same call PyPI uses to show open-issue counts).

params.name: q
params.description: GitHub issue search query, e.g. 'repo:psf/requests type:issue state:open'
